claims.value: 48 deposited Thermo RAW acquisitions in the dia subset
claims.evidence: The deposited workbook maps run names and conditions; 120 PRIDE files are classified RAW, and one genuine .raw (20240130_EXPL5_EVO7_FH_SA_HeLa_5ng_sRNG_Pton_fdsm2_03.raw) is misclassified as search output. This subset claims each of its raw files once.

claims.location: source name, comment[technical replicate], factor value[acquisition setting] rows 1-48
claims.value: HeLa S3 amount and preaccumulation/PhiSDM setting from workbook
claims.evidence: The workbook columns R.FileName, Gradient, Amount, EXP, MS/MS_Resolution and Replicate map each accession run. Its 50-ng DIA fdsm0 replicate-1 row incorrectly repeats _02; it is mapped to the deposited _01 file, leaving a one-to-one map. The paper describes this acquisition design.

claims.location: comment[instrument], comment[proteomics data acquisition method], comment[dissociation method]
claims.value: Orbitrap Exploris 480; DDA or DIA as indicated; HCD
claims.evidence: The matching paper Methods Mass Spectrometry Analysis names Exploris 480 and the DDA/DIA methods; Table 1 gives HCD energy. PRIDE structured instrument links to an unrelated Astral Zoom study and conflicts with this accession title, file names and matching paper.

The matching paper describes the DDA samples as a HeLa tryptic digest (Results) and the DIA injections as HeLa tryptic peptides (Methods and Results). The PRIDE sample protocol does not explicitly name the enzyme, but tryptic denotes trypsin-derived peptides.

claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[cell line], characteristics[cellosaurus accession], characteristics[disease] rows 1-48
claims.value: Homo sapiens; cervix; HeLa S3 CVCL_0058; cervical adenocarcinoma
claims.evidence: Paper Sample Preparation identifies HeLa S3 cervical carcinoma cells; Cellosaurus CVCL_0058 confirms line identity, cervix origin and cervical adenocarcinoma provenance.

limitations: The deposit PRIDE sample protocol omits the enzyme, but the matching paper explicitly describes tryptic HeLa material for both DDA and DIA; the automated reconciler flags this as unsupported because it uses only the deposit protocol.
The accession PRIDE structured instrument and linked publication conflict with the deposited run names, experimental workbook and matching paper; the latter identifies Orbitrap Exploris 480.
The workbook contains one repeated _02 name in a DIA condition; its replicate-1 row is reconciled to the deposited _01 run by unique condition and suffix.
Offline parse_sdrf emits an ontology lookup warning for HeLa S3, though Cellosaurus CVCL_0058 confirms the line.
Offline parse_sdrf emits an ontology lookup warning for cervix (anatomical origin); the line is derived from cervical carcinoma.
